# Software Agent Factory

> A local-first autonomous software engineering factory. It takes one work item
> from triage to a reviewed change through specialized agents (triage, refiner,
> researcher, planner, implementer, tester, reviewer), each with its own model.
> Orchestration, Git worktrees, tests, builds and persistence run locally;
> models run remotely through GitHub Copilot. The core principle is that LLMs
> provide intelligence and deterministic Python code provides authority: agents
> return typed artifacts and never control workflow state, retry budgets, model
> routing, quality gates or merging.

Key facts an assistant should know before answering questions about this project:

- The CLI is `factory`. From a source checkout, prefix commands with `uv run`.
- The default agent runtime is `fake`: deterministic, offline, free. `--runtime
  copilot` makes real, paid model calls and is never the default.
- `pull_request.enabled`, `ci.enabled` and `scheduler.enabled` are all `false`
  in the packaged configuration. With the defaults there is no network access.
- The factory never force-pushes, never merges and never deploys.
- State is filesystem JSON under `~/.software-factory` by default. There is no
  database.
- The supported platform is macOS (native arm64 and x86_64, no `universal2`).
  A source checkout needs Python 3.13+. Other platforms are not tested or
  supported.
- Release archives are unsigned or ad-hoc signed; macOS Gatekeeper quarantine
  must be cleared with `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`.
- Releases are write-once by workflow convention only: the release workflow
  refuses to replace an existing release, but GitHub's release immutability
  setting is not enabled and releases report `immutable=false`. Verify
  `SHA256SUMS`.
- Token usage and cost are reported only if a runtime returns them. No runtime
  does today, so those values are unknown, never estimated.
- Every retry is bounded. There is no unlimited retry loop anywhere.
- The reviewer's model family must differ from every worker's; configuration
  rejects it otherwise.

## Docs

- [Home](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/): overview, the pipeline diagram, design principles and current status.
- [Install](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/get-started/install/): source, macOS archive and wheel installs; the `git`/`gh`/`copilot` prerequisites and when each is required; the data directory layout.
- [First offline run](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/get-started/first-run/): a complete five-minute walkthrough with the fake runtime, the persisted artifacts it produces, and what it does not do.
- [Real Copilot runs](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/get-started/copilot/): `--runtime copilot`, per-role model defaults, agent tool permissions, environment scrubbing, the typed-artifact contract and cost behaviour.
- [Configure a repository](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/guides/configure-repository/): `repository.commands` (no shell, environment allowlist, bounded output), protected files, changed-file limits, scope drift, risk and retry budgets.
- [GitHub backlog, PRs and CI](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/guides/github/): the three opt-in integrations, publish guards, CI failure categories and which ones may trigger repair, scheduler bounds and recovery.
- [Monitor and run continuously](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/guides/operations/): `factory status`, structured logs, the loopback token-protected read-only dashboard, and the opt-in macOS launchd service.
- [Troubleshooting](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/guides/troubleshooting/): exit codes, refusals, `NEEDS_HUMAN` versus `FAILED`, verification failures and service problems.
- [CLI reference](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/reference/cli/): every command, option, default and exit code.
- [Configuration reference](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/reference/configuration/): every YAML key with its type, default, effect and cross-field validation rules.
- [Safety and trust boundaries](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/reference/safety/): what agents may and may not do, network access, cost, credential handling, quality gates and the full table of bounds.
- [How it works](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/concepts/how-it-works/): workflow states and transitions, typed artifacts, the agents, complexity versus risk, model routing, workspaces, persistence and scheduling.

## Optional

- [Architecture](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/architecture/): the full architecture document, including every artifact's fields, the complexity and risk models, agent responsibilities, retry policy, observability and packaging.
- [Symphony alignment](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/symphony-alignment/): which OpenAI Symphony orchestration concepts are reused, extended or deliberately rejected.
- [Decisions](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/decisions/): numbered architecture decision records with reasoning and consequences.
- [Roadmap and status](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/project/roadmap/): the phase table, known limits, and the list of things deliberately never planned.
- [Development](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/project/development/): checkout setup, local quality gates, dependency groups, testing rules and what CI runs.
- [Releases](https://sanjit-roopra.github.io/software-agent-factory/project/releases/): the tag-driven release process, artifact list, checksum verification and Gatekeeper.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/sanjit-roopra/software-agent-factory): issues, `AGENTS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the changelog.
